newsitem.title: MALTA: Syria says Middle East crisis threatens EU-Med ties.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Middle East crisis threatens EU-Med ties.

text.p: Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said on Wednesday the 18-month-old partnership between Europe and Mediterranean countries could be threatened by conflict in the Middle East.

Addressing a conference in Malta as the European Union battled to bring Israeli and Palestinian leaders together, Shara said regional security and stability hinged on resuming Middle East peace talks.

"It is neither realistic nor objective to speak about them if we ignore the fate of the peace process in the Middle East, the collapse of which may well lead to a probable collapse of the Barcelona process."

The Barcelona process forged in 1995 created a partnership between 15 European states and 12 Mediterranean partners, including Arab countries, the Palestinian Authority and Israel. The Malta conference is a followup to Barcelona.
Shara referred to the original Barcelona declaration which focused on the principle of "land for peace" in the process to end decades of conflict in the Middle East.

"These countries are now called upon to take a clear stand that helps to serve the peace process which is threatened with collapse due to the policies of the Israeli government which are hostile to peace."
The Syrian minister said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had rejected the principle of land for peace, and was pursuing Jewish settlement and confiscation of occupied Arab territory.

"A firm stand by the European Union supported by practical measures taken vis-a-vis the Israeli policies and practices would certainly help salvage the peace process and put it back on track," he said.
He repeated Syria's willingness to return to peace talks, broken off a year ago, provided they resumed at the same point.
Talks then were with the previous Labour-led government, which he said had agreed in principle to return the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. Netanyahu opposes giving up occupied land.

Shara said Syria's "strategic option" for peace required full Israeli withdrawal in the Golan to the line of June 4, 1967, from south Lebanon, and the Palestinian occupied territories, including East Jerusalem.
